new.question: Is spending on track?
new.text:
Across the 20-Gram-Panchayat sample, the spending-against-plan balance for costed activities is Rs -51.96 crore, indicating recorded spending below plan; no single Gram Panchayat accounts for most of this balance. Biswamathpur accounts for 13.9% (Rs -7.23 crore) while holding 4.3% of the 5,630 activities, and Kalimela accounts for 11.3% (Rs -5.90 crore).

Below-plan spending is also visible across major themes. The balance is Rs -20.13 crore for Theme 6—Self-sufficient Infrastructure, led by Sharagada at 16.7% (Rs -3.36 crore) and Biswamathpur at 13.2% (Rs -2.66 crore). For Theme 4—Water Sufficient Village, it is Rs -13.11 crore, with Kalimela accounting for 25.5% (Rs -3.34 crore) and Boipariguda for 10.1% (Rs -1.32 crore). For Theme 5—Clean and Green Village, it is Rs -8.62 crore, with Biswamathpur accounting for 25.0% (Rs -2.15 crore) and Bheden for 10.9% (Rs -93.73 lakh).

The next review should prioritise reconciliation of plans, sanctions and recorded payments in Biswamathpur, Kalimela and Sharagada, where shares of the below-plan balance are notably larger than their shares of activities in the relevant groupings. The remaining gaps are spread across the other Gram Panchayats, so broader follow-up is also warranted rather than treating the issue as confined to a few locations.

(as of 2026-08-17)

new.question: How is Chikilli doing?
new.text:
Within the 20-Gram-Panchayat sample, Chikilli has the lowest sanctioned amount across all fiscal years. It also records the fewest activities with technical and administrative approval in 5/6 fiscal years; 2023-2024 is the exception, with no clear pattern.

Recorded spending is Rs 4.12 crore below plan across 28 focus areas. Maintenance of community systems accounts for 23.9% (Rs -98.63 lakh) of this gap and roads for 18.0% (Rs -74.02 lakh), while the other 26 areas account for Rs -2.39 crore. Planned money associated with abandoned works totals Rs 46.72 lakh, including 43.7% (Rs 20.44 lakh) under Theme 6—Self-sufficient Infrastructure in Village and 33.8% (Rs 15.77 lakh) under Theme 5—Clean and Green Village.

Spending linked to planned activities totals Rs 1.30 crore across 6 fiscal years, and the linked share increased from 2.7% to 53.2%. This increase indicates improved linkage in the records unless cashbook totals rose alongside it, so Chikilli’s sanctions, approvals, plan-to-spending reconciliation and abandoned-work records merit review together.

(as of 2026-08-17)

new.question: How is Barpali block doing?
new.text:
Barpali records Rs 2.64 crore in spending, accounting for 48.4% of the Rs 5.44 crore recorded across three blocks in Bargarh district. Within Barpali’s two Gram Panchayats and 1,447 activities, planned cost totals Rs 5.49 crore and spending totals Rs 2.64 crore; Bandhpali accounts for 61.0% of planned cost and 53.1% of spending, while Bhatigaon accounts for 39.0% and 46.9%, respectively. Ongoing works are similarly distributed, with 88 activities in Bhatigaon and 83 in Bandhpali, out of 171. 

Abandoned works warrant closer attention in Bandhpali: it holds Rs 70.66 lakh, or 75.4%, of Barpali’s Rs 93.72 lakh in planned money on abandoned works, compared with Rs 23.06 lakh in Bhatigaon. Spending linked to planned activities totals Rs 2.55 crore, split between Bandhpali at Rs 1.34 crore and Bhatigaon at Rs 1.20 crore; the linked share rose from 2.7% to 53.2% across six years, which should be reviewed alongside cashbook totals when assessing recording completeness.

(as of 2026-08-17)

new.question: Tell me about untied grants.
new.text:
Recorded untied-grant plans total Rs 16.95 crore across 19 Gram Panchayats, with no single GP standing out. Sharagada has the largest share at 8.5% (Rs 1.44 crore), followed by Kalimela at 7.1% (Rs 1.21 crore); the remaining 17 account for Rs 14.30 crore. Sharagada holds 4.1% of the 1,088 planned activities, compared with 8.5% of the planned amount. 

The planned use is broadly consistent across Gram Panchayats: Codes 101 and 105 lead among output types in 19/20, with Haldikudar showing a different pattern. Theme 6—Self-sufficient Infrastructure in Village—has the highest planned amount in 18/20; Boipariguda is led by the Unmapped LSDG theme, while Kalimela is led by Theme 4—Water Sufficient Village. New/Fresh works have the highest planned amount in 16/20; Maintenance leads in Sharagada, while Barimunda, Hirlipali and one other Gram Panchayat show different patterns.

(as of 2026-08-17)

new.question: Anything I should be looking at in Ganjam?
new.text:
Ganjam’s records merit reconciliation between plans, sanctions and spending. Across 4 Gram Panchayats, spending measured against plan is Rs -17.85 crore, indicating spending below plan; Biswamathpur accounts for Rs -7.23 crore and Sharagada for Rs -4.63 crore, while the remaining 2 account for Rs -6.00 crore. 

Sanction records cover only about one in six activities, limiting interpretation of the Rs 6.30 crore sanctioned total. At block level, Rangeilunda records Rs 3.56 crore, Sheragada Rs 2.74 crore and Khallikote Rs 0. Spending linked to planned activities totals Rs 5.65 crore across 6 fiscal years, while the linked share rose from 2.7% to 53.2%; this should be treated as improved recording completeness unless cashbook totals show a corresponding rise. 

Sharagada merits a specific check on abandoned works: it accounts for 62.1% of the Rs 1.91 crore planned for abandoned works, or Rs 1.19 crore, across the 4 Gram Panchayats. Its sanctions are also the largest Gram Panchayat share at 43.5%, or Rs 2.74 crore.

(as of 2026-08-17)

new.question: What is the position on abandoned works?
new.text:
Abandoned works carry planned expenditure of Rs 5.85 crore across 18 Gram Panchayats in the sample. No single GP dominates: Sharagada has the largest share at 20.3% (Rs 1.19 crore), followed by Bheden at 15.0% (Rs 87.81 lakh), while the remaining 16 account for Rs 3.78 crore. Sharagada represents 4.5% of the 420 abandoned activities but 20.3% of the associated planned money, making its records particularly relevant for review.

Among districts, Bargarh has the highest number of abandoned activities across work types. Sanitation records the highest number among focus areas in 5/6 fiscal years; 2020-2021 is the exception, with no clear pattern. New/Fresh works similarly rank highest among work types in 5/6 fiscal years, while Maintenance ranks highest in 2022-2023.

(as of 2026-08-17)
